findings.message: The redirect read path is the highest-traffic path and the primary SLO (p95 < 50 ms, @threshold:PRD.01.perf.redirectp95), yet the monitoring baseline table contains no row for redirect read-path latency. An on-call engineer reading §7 cannot see the signal for the most latency-sensitive operation. The fixer added the write-conflict threshold and the durable-commit row, but the read path remains invisible in the monitoring table — meaning a latency regression on the hot path would surface only through end-user complaints or an external synthetic monitor, not through an ADR-declared metric and alert.
findings.recommendation: Add a monitoring row: metric = redirect read-path latency (p95), target = < 50 ms (@threshold:PRD.01.perf.redirectp95), alert threshold = >= 50 ms sustained over a calibration window (e.g., 2 min). This closes the observability gap on the primary SLO without requiring a new system — the same KV client instrumentation that reports commit latency can report read latency.

findings.message: Visit-count reconciliation lag has no monitoring row or alert threshold. BDD.01.03.a7ad establishes a 60 s reconciliation budget and the ADR acknowledges reconciliation logging as the durability backstop for off-path dropped increments (ADR.01.05.9107, §3 off-path increment). A stuck or lagging reconciliation process would be silent under the current monitoring baseline: the only signal is confirmed-mapping loss (RPO) = any loss, which fires only after the failure has propagated to mapping durability — too late to act on a count-reconciliation fault. The consequence is undercounted visit metrics and a potential BRD.01.10.7d5a (visit count confirmed-write durable) violation without alerting.
findings.recommendation: Add a monitoring row: metric = reconciliation lag (age of oldest unresolved dropped-increment log entry), target = < 60 s (aligned to BDD.01.03.a7ad reconciliation budget), alert threshold = >= 60 s -> WARN. The reconciliation log already exists per the decision; instrumenting its oldest-entry age closes the observability gap with no architectural change.

notes: C1 satisfied by one-way exemption; voluntary 7-step runbook is present and operationally sound (fixer resolved OPS-P3-001). Write-conflict alert threshold is now quantified at > 5 conflicts/min over 5 min (fixer resolved OPS-P3-002). C3 satisfied by the 3-phase MVP sequencing with explicit ordering rationale. C4 satisfied by order-of-magnitude cost in §4 and §5. C5 N/A (non-toggleable one-way decision). Two P2 gaps remain: redirect read-path latency (primary SLO) and reconciliation-lag age are absent from the monitoring baseline.
